history.origins: Tiến lên is a shedding-type card game originating in Vietnam and is often considered Vietnam's national card game. It is common in Vietnamese and Vietnamese-American communities and spread to the United States and Australia with migration. It is related to Chinese climbing games such as Big Two and Dou dizhu.
timeline: 20th century: Evolved in Vietnam from Chinese climbing games; spread with diaspora.
history.cultural: Extremely popular in Vietnam and Vietnamese-American communities.
history.evolution: Spread to the West with the Vietnamese diaspora.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card. Rank: 3(low)-4-5...K-A-2(high). Suit Rank: Spades < Clubs < Diamonds < Hearts.
setup.dealing: Deal all 13 cards to each player.

rules.objective: Be the first player to shed all cards from your hand; the last player left holding any cards loses the game.
rules.gameplay: First round: Player with 3 Spades starts. Subsequent: Winner of last round starts. Play combination (Single, Pair, Triple, Run). Next player must beat it with same type and higher rank/suit. Pass = out for the trick. 2s are high. 'Bombs' (4-of-a-kind, double runs) can beat 2s out of turn (Chopping). Winner is first out. Others play for 2nd, etc., or game ends.
keyRules: Must beat with same number of cards (usually)

strategy.basic: Save 2s for control. Get rid of small singles early. Break pairs if needed to gain lead.
strategy.intermediate: Use bombs (chop) to catch opponents' 2s for big points/control. Bait out 2s.
strategy.advanced: Card counting (especially 2s and Aces). Memorizing played suits to know if your Heart is the 'Nut' (highest remaining).
tips: Don't get stuck with a 2 at the end (rotting).
A sequence of 3-4-5 is weak but useful to shed small cards.
Control the lead to dictate the game type (pairs vs singles).

scoring.description: Losers pay winner. Penalties for holding 2s or bombs when game ends (rotting). 'Insta-win' hands exist (e.g. 4 Twos, Dragon straight).
scoring.winCondition: Be the first to shed all cards.
